title: Your snacks, the science of baking, and food safety

say: Your snacks, the science of baking, and food safety.
This is the video for module one of Basic Baking and Snacks Production.

At any school gate or motor park in Nigeria, you see the same snacks: meat pie, chin chin, puff-puff, bread and cake. Chin chin and puff-puff are fried in hot oil. They need only a stove and a deep pot, so they are the cheapest way to start.

panel.heading: Fried or baked?
left: Needs only a stove and a deep pot

say: Bread, cake and meat pie are baked in an oven. They need more equipment, but usually sell at a higher price per piece.

panel.heading: Fried or baked?
left: Needs only a stove and a deep pot

say: Shelf life is how long a product stays safe and pleasant to eat. Puff-puff and meat pie spoil fast. You cook in the morning and sell by afternoon.

panel.heading: How fast it spoils decides how you sell

Chin chin: pack sealed, sell slowly

say: A recipe is not magic. Flour and water form gluten, a stretchy net. Kneading makes it strong, so bread traps gas and rises. For pastry and cake, mix gently, so the bite stays tender.

panel.heading: Every ingredient has a job
items: Flour: kneading builds stretchy gluten
Yeast: alive, needs warmth and time
Baking powder: works when wet and heated
Fat: shortens gluten, keeps things soft
Sugar browns; eggs bind and set; salt

say: Yeast is a living fungus. It eats sugar and gives off gas, but it needs warmth and time. Very hot water kills it.

say: Baking powder releases gas when wet and again when heated. Baking soda only works with an acid, like yoghurt or lemon juice.

say: For example, Amaka's puff-puff batter did not rise, and the balls fried flat and heavy. First she checks the yeast. The sachet was opened two months ago and left in a hot kitchen.

panel.heading: Why Amaka's puff-puff fried flat
items: Yeast sachet opened two months ago
Water just off the boil
Fresh yeast, lukewarm water
Covered, warm spot: doubled in 45 minutes

say: Then the water. She used water just off the boil, because the morning was cold. That killed the yeast.

say: When you sell food, customers trust you with their health. Follow the World Health Organization's Five Keys.
Keep clean. Wash hands with soap before handling food, and after the toilet, raw meat, money or your phone. Separate raw and cooked. Use a separate board and knife for raw meat.
Cook thoroughly. Cook meat filling on the stove until no pink remains, at least 70 degrees Celsius at the centre.
Keep food out of the danger zone, between 5 and 60 degrees, and never more than 2 hours at room temperature. And use safe water, good flour and uncracked eggs.

panel.heading: WHO Five Keys to Safer Food
items: Keep clean
Separate raw and cooked
Cook thoroughly
Keep food at safe temperatures
Use safe water and raw materials

say: Never leave hot oil unattended, and keep children away from the stove. Lower food into the oil gently, away from you.

cards.d: Keep children away. Lower food into oil gently with a spoon, away from you.
Turn off the gas if safe and cover the pot with a lid. Never pour water on an oil fire.
Keep it upright and ventilated. Check hoses for leaks with soapy water, not a flame.

say: If oil catches fire, turn off the gas if you can reach it safely, and cover the pot with a lid or fire blanket. Never pour water on an oil fire.

say: So remember. Fried snacks need only a stove. Short shelf life means make close to the time of sale. Yeast needs lukewarm water and time.
Follow the Five Keys. And the most important tool for repeatable baking is a digital scale.

panel.heading: Key points
items: Fried needs a stove; baked needs an oven
Short shelf life: make close to sale
Yeast needs lukewarm water and time
Follow the WHO Five Keys
A digital scale is your key tool
